findings.criterion: One-time setup burden versus real recruiter fallback
findings.observation: The release candidate now clears the honesty and setup-discipline bar for exposure. It teaches the exact two-action personal Shortcut, names the primary control for what it actually does, keeps generic App Shortcuts separate, and avoids a fake one-tap install claim. It remains a 3 rather than a 4 because the one-time setup burden is proven by aligned simulator evidence, not by first-time recruiter completion on physical Action Button devices.
findings.evidence: artifact-r7.md freezes product commit c43145222c7750bf5cfc705384e46ce694f325df and all 15 listed hashes; I recomputed every listed SHA-256 on 2026-09-04 and all matched. /tmp/talent-signal-action-button-c431452.xcresult reports 26 tests and succeeded. Screenshot 3CCAE38B-A080-47A9-8E02-AA93CEF28919.png shows the recruiter-visible setup loop: Take Screenshot, Review screenshot, Local before you decide, and Open Shortcut editor. Screenshot 9BE3703B-4A2E-41A1-96E3-A75CA7BFD4F0.png shows the entry labeled Set up quick capture with One-time setup. Dimension scores from the r7 evidence: trigger relevance=3, capture burden=3, evidence review=3, state integrity=3, action usefulness=3, write safety=3, interruption recovery=3, wedge discipline=3.
findings.user_impact: A time-constrained independent recruiter can set this up without being misled about what the app or iOS is doing, but the team still lacks direct proof that first-time users finish the setup faster than their existing workaround under live-search interruption.
findings.recommendation: Keep the current setup surface and validate it in the field instead of redesigning it again. Measure first-pass completion, detours into Other shortcuts, and abandonment on physical Action Button devices.
findings.verification: On physical Action Button iPhones, have first-time recruiters start from a fresh install and reach first successful screenshot capture with no coaching. Record completion rate, detours, time-to-first-success, and whether they can restate the Assigned versus Local receipt boundary.

findings.observation: The receipt state is now operationally trustworthy. Local receipt is distinct from Assigned, Screenshot received via Shortcuts explicitly limits what was observed, and the unchecked assignment control stays visible. The recruiter can safely resume on next launch and choose keep or discard before processing. The remaining friction is that the receipt surface still communicates status more than it accelerates the next review step.
findings.evidence: CandidateSignalUITests.swift asserts that with action-button-complete NO and screenshot-shortcut-received-at set, the settings row contains Local receipt, the detail label is Screenshot received via Shortcuts, and Action Button Ready is absent. Screenshot 5638E563-863E-488F-BC6E-5FAA0459495C.png shows the unchecked I've assigned the Shortcut control above the receipt card and the footer saying the receipt does not prove the current Action Button assignment. Screenshot 5B7E88EB-5F57-4D6A-9567-D4DC36EC8184.png shows the preserved keep-or-discard gate before processing, and RelationshipCaptureTests.swift covers queue persistence, exact-retry deduplication, later re-import, deletion, unresolved identity, and retry without repeating the identity decision.
findings.user_impact: The recruiter no longer risks mistaking an app-owned receipt for hardware verification or confirmed state, and their work survives interruption. They may still spend an extra navigation step getting from yes, it arrived to the oldest pending screenshot review.
findings.recommendation: When pending capture count is greater than zero, let the Local receipt state expose one direct Review pending screenshot action without changing the current truth boundary or assignment semantics.
findings.verification: Seed queued screenshots, open the Action Button & Shortcuts surface from the Local receipt state, and verify that a direct review action opens the oldest queued capture, preserves FIFO order, and leaves Assigned unchanged.

strengths: The r7 review packet is genuinely frozen: all listed hashes matched at review time, the immutable product commit resolved to c43145222c7750bf5cfc705384e46ce694f325df, and the cited xcresult bundle directly reports 26 passed tests and 0 failed.

The product tells the truth about platform limits. Only the user assigns the Shortcut in Settings, the app cannot read or change the Action Button binding, and Review screenshot is not advertised as a one-step App Shortcut.

The capture-to-review loop is narrow and recruiter-appropriate: capture one authorized conversation, stage it locally, preserve evidence and reviewed draft, then keep, discard, or explicitly continue to Save and check identity.

The rejection path is materially safer in r7: corrupt, over-25-MiB, and over-80-megapixel input is rejected before both queue persistence and receipt creation, which reduces misleading local receipts and cleanup work.
Chinese AX5 evidence remains aligned with the release candidate, including the setup hierarchy and the separate source-settings entry for Local receipt.
missing_evidence: No connected physical iPhone was available, so current Action Button mapping and physical press remain an explicit evidence boundary rather than a product failure.
No first-time recruiter field study yet shows actual setup completion rate, abandonment rate, or measured time saved versus the recruiter's manual fallback.
The receipt status surface does not yet prove a one-tap jump into the oldest queued review item; the release candidate proves safe resume and keep/discard recovery instead.
open_questions: Do first-time recruiters understand Local receipt immediately, or do some still infer broader Action Button verification before opening the detail?
After physical-device validation, does the Other shortcuts section help discovery or create extra setup detours for recruiters who only want screenshot capture?
